question: What can push inflation away from a central bank's target, according to the guest?
gold_answer: A surge in demand in the economy (for example from a large inflow of foreign money), or government programmes that add to demand.
key_points: demand boom; foreign money inflows; government programmes
author: claude

question: What was the IMF originally created to be, and what test decides whether it lends to a country?
gold_answer: It was created to be a financial firefighter. It lends if it has confidence that the country's new government will move the country away from the abyss.
author: claude

question: Which questions does the guest suggest putting to an AI assistant to find channel partners for a product?
gold_answer: Which markets the product is used in, who the customers are, and through which channels they get access to such services; then ask for a profile of 10 to 20 companies.
author: claude

question: What does the guest say about small businesses and the five-year mark?
gold_answer: Around half of small businesses do not survive five years, so you must understand your unit economics, entry cost and payback period, not only sales.
key_points: 50% fail by five years; unit economics; payback period
author: claude

question: What does Vinh Giang give as the first step to communicating better?
gold_answer: Become self-aware: you have never seen yourself communicate, and your view of how you come across is not accurate.
key_points: self-awareness; your view is not accurate
author: claude

question: When does he say you should write down a story you might tell later?
gold_answer: Whenever something emotionally moves you, grab your phone and document it straight away; the biggest rule of storytelling is to document.
key_points: document when emotionally moved; use your phone
author: claude

question: Where does Josh Woodward say the best new product ideas at Labs actually come from?
gold_answer: Rarely from design sprints or scheduled idea sessions. They come when people are hacking and building on their own, in the hallway, on weekends or over a break, and then share a video.
key_points: not design sprints; hacking on weekends and breaks
author: claude

question: What happened when the team saw early data on a Gemini feature they had been excited about?
gold_answer: People looked users in the eye and it wasn't working, and a PM on the team said she didn't think they should launch it. He was proud of her for saying so.
key_points: early data weak; PM spoke up; did not launch
author: claude

question: How often does the guest tell a prospect that the gap between them is simply too big?
gold_answer: About one in every four calls. In two to three of every four there is something real.
key_points: one in four calls; revisit in a year
author: claude

question: How should a software price relate to the length of the sales cycle, in the guest's view?
gold_answer: Price should be based on the sales cycle: if you can close in 90 days for 100K, do that every time; a deal that takes nine months should be priced higher.
key_points: price follows sales cycle; 90 days for 100K
author: claude

question: What should you do when the customer's lawyers return extensive redlines on the contract?
gold_answer: Accept the easy changes, and try to get legal on a live call to talk through the rest, which speeds up the sales cycle.
key_points: accept easy items; get legal on a call
author: claude

question: What does Rob Snyder mean by a hair-on-fire problem?
gold_answer: An urgent, concretely defined problem, such as a to-do that your boss is waiting for and that must happen now.
author: claude

question: What kind of reaction from a prospect shows genuine interest, and what shows only polite interest?
gold_answer: Leaning in ('wait, you can do what?' or 'I will pay you right now') is the signal. Leaned-out enthusiasm ('tell me more', 'send some information for the team to review') is not worth chasing.
author: claude

question: What is an agent harness, as explained in the course?
gold_answer: The platform that runs the loop: a model that keeps going until the task is done, connected to your tools and your context. Popular agent products are agent harnesses.
key_points: loop until done; tools and context; popular agents are harnesses
author: claude

question: How is a skill different from keeping something in an agent's memory?
gold_answer: A skill packages a whole process as a markdown file (for example writing a proposal) so it is done the same way each time; memory holds preferences and facts. Process material clogs memory and belongs in skills.
author: claude

question: What does the speaker say happens to the work that UGC creators, video editors and motion designers used to do for ads?
gold_answer: That work is now handled by an AI agent tool; marketing is becoming code, software and tokens.
key_points: agents replace creator, editor, motion designer; marketing is code
author: claude

question: How does the guest connect his bot to Claude Code?
gold_answer: Easy way: tell the bot to log into Claude Code on its own computer. His way: a network of machines connected through Tailscale, using T3 Code.

question: What did the guest's bot do when he bought a PS5 Pro?
gold_answer: It emailed the eBay seller, negotiated for him and checked that the console was viable.

question: Why does the guest's company rely mostly on prompts rather than fine-tuning?
gold_answer: Because prompting is easy and portable; about 98% of their value comes from prompts.

question: What does the host say is ending in software?
gold_answer: The era of dumb tools and dumb SaaS, where a human goes and presses buttons and uploads data to a CRM.

question: What do the guests say about working closely with early customers, even by hand, before trying to scale?
gold_answer: Rob Snyder says starting as a service, with humans doing the work by hand and automation built up around it, can work, though you can get stuck as a services business. key_points: start by hand; one first client; do not scale too early

question: What do the guests say about using content to get a product noticed?
gold_answer: Sachin Puri suggests a small business build content around real success stories of founders, and says AI can now produce that content. The speaker in the $1M solo business episode says to make content about your product because people will eventually try it once they have seen you enough.
key_points: success-story content; AI can make it; keep making content

question: What examples do the guests give of agents repeatedly checking for things on their own?

key_points: car marketplaces every three hours; morning briefing; eBay listings every day

question: How do the guests say AI is changing marketing and creative work?
gold_answer: In 'AI Agents are too good at marketing now', the speaker says marketing is now just code, software and tokens, and the work of UGC creators, editors and motion designers is handled by bots. In the AI wrappers episode the guest says a top 1% marketing engineer covers SEO, GEO, social and paid ads and has an unfair advantage, while the other 98% risk becoming dinosaurs.
key_points: marketing is code; creators replaced by bots; top 1% marketing engineer
author: claude

question: What do the guests say about the human abilities that matter as AI takes over routine work?
gold_answer: Josh Woodward looks for people with a high unlearning rate, who can learn something and then walk away from it, as well as learning rate and endurance. Sachin Puri says routine data analysis will shrink and people will move to higher-order understanding of the questions to ask. Gita Gopinath tells students not to skip working with classmates now that a brilliant classmate sits on their phone.
key_points: unlearning rate; higher-order questions; keep working with people
author: claude

question: How do the guests say you can tell a prospect is not a good fit?
gold_answer: Jen Abel says that on about one in four calls the gap between the prospect's maturity and hers is too big, so she suggests revisiting in a year. Rob Snyder says you can tell prospects they do not look like your case study, so it will be a lot of work and might not be a good fit.
key_points: gap too big; revisit later; does not look like a case study
author: claude

question: What do the guests say about how and when to charge customers?
gold_answer: Jen Abel says price should follow the sales cycle, for example closing in 90 days at 100K, and that for a 30-day value case you charge and credit it back. question: How do the guests describe giving an AI agent the context it needs?
gold_answer: The AI Agents Full Course says an agent harness connects the model to your tools and all the context, with memory that builds over time. key_points: harness connects context; memory builds up; get context from the user

question: What do the guests say about building software quickly with AI coding agents?

question: How do the guests suggest deciding who to approach first when selling or distributing a product?

question: How do the guests get AI agents to produce work that matches a particular look?

author: claude

question: How do different guests describe what an agent harness is or why it matters?
gold_answer: The AI Agents Full Course defines it as the platform that runs the loop, with a model that keeps going until the task is done, connected to tools and context. In the wrappers episode the guest says the whole game is harness building: get the right context, express the output well, and distil it so an off-the-shelf model does well.

question: What role does a friendly contact or champion inside the buyer's company play in closing a deal?
